claims.text: Setting the environment variable PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
A page exists at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ describing the Terraform/OpenTofu state backend for Pulumi Cloud.
The self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service accepts an environment variable named PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN that specifies the domain serving the Terraform-compatible API.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes are not registered.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN for the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, so a separate domain for the Terraform-compatible API is not required.
The Pulumi Cloud Terraform state backend guide uses tf.pulumi.com as the domain in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the TF_TOKEN_* variable name.

For a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value must be used in the Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, in the `terraform login` or `tofu login` command, and in the TF_TOKEN_* variable name.
